title: Kanamycin detection at graphene quantum dot-decorated gold nanoparticles in organized medium after solid-phase extraction using an aminoglycoside imprinted polymer
author: Toloza, Almeida, et al.
materials: Stock standard solutions of analyte were prepared at 1.0 × 10−2 mol L−1 and at 1.0 mmol L−1 by the direct dilution of appropriate amounts of kanamycin sulfate in ultrapure water. Less concentrated standard solutions were prepared by diluting the stock solutions with water. Sample solutions of the pharmaceutical formulations and samples of yellow fever vaccine were prepared only by successive dilutions of the original sample, prior to SPE.

steps.title: Synthesize kanamycin‑imprinted polymer (MIP)
steps.instruction: Prepare the sol‑gel MIP by dissolving kanamycin sulfate, adding reagents, heating, curing, crushing, washing, drying and sieving.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 500 mg kanamycin sulfate in 6 mL deionised water.
Add 400 µL of 1 mol L⁻¹ aqueous HCl (catalyst).
Add 3200 µL of (3‑aminopropyl)trimethoxysilane (APTMS).
Add 2650 µL of tetraethyl orthosilicate (TEOS).
Heat the mixture to 40 °C and continue heating until the solution just turns turbid.
Maintain the temperature at 40 °C with controlled stirring for 5 min.
Cool the resulting gel to room temperature and let it stand for 12 h to ensure dryness.
Crush the dried gel with a mortar and pestle.
Wash the crushed material with 1 L warm deionised water, then with 300 mL methanol to extract the kanamycin template.
Repeat the water‑then‑methanol washing two additional times (total three washes).
Monitor the removal of kanamycin by measuring the photoluminescence response of the AuNP‑amino‑GQD‑CTAB probe.
Dry the cleaned polymer in a desiccator.
Pass the dried polymer through a molecular sieve and collect particles sized 106–150 µm.
Store the final MIP at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare non‑imprinted polymer (NIP)
steps.instruction: Synthesize a control polymer using the same sol‑gel procedure but omit the kanamycin template.

steps.title: Perform solid‑phase extraction (SPE)
steps.instruction: Use a FIAlab‑2500 flow‑injection system to pass solvents through the MIP cartridge at a constant flow rate for conditioning, cleaning, and elution steps.

steps.title: Prepare AuNP‑amino‑GQD‑CTAB working dispersion
steps.instruction: Make 5 mL analytical probe solutions containing the nanoprobes and kanamycin (or blank).

substeps.instruction: Pipette 1.50 mL of the AuNP‑amino‑GQD‑CTAB dispersion into a 5.00 mL volumetric flask.
Add the required volume (µL‑scale) of a kanamycin standard solution or sample.
Fill to the mark with ultrapure water to reach a final volume of 5.00 mL.
Allow the mixture to stand at room temperature for 30 min before measuring photoluminescence.
For blank dispersions, add only ultrapure water to reach 5.00 mL (no kanamycin).

steps.title: Prepare kanamycin sulfate standards and samples
steps.instruction: Create stock solutions and dilute them to obtain calibration standards and sample extracts.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 1.0 × 10⁻² mol L⁻¹ stock solution of kanamycin sulfate by dissolving the appropriate mass in ultrapure water.
Prepare a 1.0 mmol L⁻¹ stock solution of kanamycin sulfate similarly.
Generate lower‑concentration standards by diluting either stock solution with ultrapure water to the desired concentration.
Prepare sample solutions of pharmaceutical formulations and yellow‑fever vaccine by successive dilutions of the original sample (performed before SPE).

description: Previous work has shown the importance of the indirect determination of kanamycin sulfate using semiconductor quantum dots and gold nanoparticles [1]. In this paper, a recently published experimental procedure, used to the selective determination of kanamycin sulfate [2], is reported. The indirect determination was made by measuring the photoluminescence response of an off-on probe based on spherical gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) decorated with amino-functionalized graphene quantum dots (amino-GQDs) obtained from the exfoliation of a mixture of citric acid and glutathione (GSH) in an aqueous solution containing hexadecyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB). The CTAB is used as a bridge to facilitate the approximation of the negatively charged AuNPs on the surface and the amino-GQDs, which are also negatively charged. The presence of CTAB in the AuNPs-amino-GQDs system also helped to improve the interaction of kanamycin with the nanostructure [2]. In the presence of kanamycin sulfate, the signal of a photoluminescence suppressed nanoparticle system (AuNPs-amino-GQDs-CTAB) was restored. Characterization of the AuNP-amino-GQD-CTAB system [2] and the optimization of its synthesis are reported in this paper. Solid-phase extraction using a laboratory-made kanamycin sulfate imprinted polymer was used to facilitate previous separation of analyte from samples and offer selectivity by the method.
